questions.question: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
answer_steps: Let $AB$ be a diameter, with tangents $l$ at $A$ and $m$ at $B$.
$OA \perp l$ and $OB \perp m$ (radius ⊥ tangent), so both tangents are perpendicular to the line $AB$.
Lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel, so $l \parallel m$.

questions.question: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. Prove that $AB + CD = AD + BC$.
answer_steps: Let the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$ touch the circle at $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$.
Tangents from a point are equal: $AP = AS$, $BP = BQ$, $CR = CQ$, $DR = DS$.
Adding: $AB + CD = (AP + PB) + (CR + RD) = AS + BQ + CQ + DS = AD + BC$.

questions.question: XY and X′Y′ are two parallel tangents to a circle with centre O and another tangent AB with point of contact C intersecting XY at A and X′Y′ at B. Prove that $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$.
answer_steps: Let $XY$ and $X'Y'$ touch the circle at $P$ and $Q$; $PQ$ is a diameter. $\triangle OPA \cong \triangle OCA$ (RHS), so $\angle POA = \angle COA$.
Similarly $\triangle OQB \cong \triangle OCB$, so $\angle QOB = \angle COB$.
$\angle POA + \angle COA + \angle COB + \angle QOB = 180^\circ$, so $2(\angle COA + \angle COB) = 180^\circ$ and $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$.
marking_scheme: 1 mark: figure with radii to the points of contact
1 mark: correct reasons (radius ⊥ tangent / equal tangents)

questions.question: Prove that the angle between the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is supplementary to the angle subtended by the line-segment joining the points of contact at the centre.
answer_steps: Let $PA$ and $PB$ be the tangents from $P$, touching the circle with centre $O$ at $A$ and $B$.
$\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ$ (radius ⊥ tangent).
In quadrilateral $OAPB$: $\angle AOB + \angle APB = 360^\circ - 180^\circ = 180^\circ$.

questions.question: Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
answer_steps: For the circumscribing parallelogram $ABCD$, equal tangents give $AB + CD = AD + BC$.
In a parallelogram $AB = CD$ and $AD = BC$, so $2AB = 2AD$, i.e. $AB = AD$.
A parallelogram with two adjacent sides equal is a rhombus.

questions.question: Prove that opposite sides of a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle subtend supplementary angles at the centre of the circle.
answer_steps: Join $O$ to the vertices and to the points of contact. Congruent triangles (RHS) at each vertex give equal pairs of angles at $O$: call them $a, a, b, b, c, c, d, d$.
Their sum is $360^\circ$, so $a + b + c + d = 180^\circ$.
$\angle AOB + \angle COD = (a + b) + (c + d) = 180^\circ$, and similarly $\angle BOC + \angle DOA = 180^\circ$.

1 mark: correct reasons (radius ⊥ tangent / equal tangents)

questions.question: A triangle ABC is drawn to circumscribe a circle of radius 4 cm such that the segments BD and DC into which BC is divided by the point of contact D are of lengths 8 cm and 6 cm respectively. Find the sides AB and AC.
answer_steps: Equal tangents: $BF = BD = 8$, $CE = CD = 6$, and let $AE = AF = x$.
Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times (\text{perimeter}) = 4(14 + x)$.
By Heron's formula, area $= \sqrt{(14 + x) \cdot x \cdot 6 \cdot 8}$. Squaring: $48x(14 + x) = 16(14 + x)^{2}$, so $3x = 14 + x$ and $x = 7$.
$AB = 15$ cm and $AC = 13$ cm

questions.question: Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
answer_steps: Let the tangent $XY$ touch the circle with centre $O$ at $P$. Take any point $Q$ on $XY$ other than $P$, and join $OQ$.
$Q$ lies outside the circle (the tangent meets the circle only at $P$), so $OQ > OP$.
So $OP$ is the shortest of all the segments from $O$ to points of $XY$, and the shortest such segment is perpendicular to the line: $OP \perp XY$.

1 mark: correct reasons (radius ⊥ tangent / equal tangents)

questions.question: Prove that the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
answer_steps: Let $PQ$ and $PR$ be tangents from $P$ to the circle with centre $O$. Join $OP$, $OQ$ and $OR$.
In $\triangle OQP$ and $\triangle ORP$: $OQ = OR$ (radii), $OP$ is common and $\angle OQP = \angle ORP = 90^\circ$ (radius ⊥ tangent).
So $\triangle OQP \cong \triangle ORP$ (RHS), and $PQ = PR$ (CPCT).

questions.question: Two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point P. Prove that $\angle APB = 2\angle OAB$.
answer_steps: Let $\angle APB = \theta$. $PA = PB$ (tangents from an external point), so $\angle PAB = \angle PBA = 90^\circ - \dfrac{\theta}{2}$.
$\angle OAP = 90^\circ$ (radius ⊥ tangent), so $\angle OAB = 90^\circ - \angle PAB = \dfrac{\theta}{2}$.
Hence $\angle APB = 2\angle OAB$.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a right-angled triangle ABC, right-angled at B. If BC = 7 cm and AB = 24 cm, find the radius of the circle.

questions.question: Prove that the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. Hence, if a quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle with AB = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm and CD = 12 cm, find AD.

$OQ = OR$ (radii), $OP$ common, $\angle OQP = \angle ORP = 90^\circ$, so $\triangle OQP \cong \triangle ORP$ (RHS) and $PQ = PR$.
For $ABCD$, equal tangents from each vertex give $AB + CD = AD + BC$.

questions.question: A triangle ABC circumscribes a circle of radius 3 cm. The point of contact D divides BC into BD = 6 cm and DC = 9 cm. If the area of the triangle is 54 cm², find AB and AC, and show that the triangle is right-angled.
answer_steps: Equal tangents: let $AE = AF = x$; then $AB = x + 6$, $AC = x + 9$, $BC = 15$.
Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times (\text{perimeter}) = 3(15 + x)$.
$AB = 9$ cm, $AC = 12$ cm

questions.question:
A circular garden has radius 5 m and centre O. From a gate P, 13 m from O, two straight paths PA and PB touch the garden's boundary at A and B.

(i) Find the length of the path PA. (1)

(ii) Without calculating again, find PB. Give the reason. (1)

(iii) Find the area of the quadrilateral OAPB. OR Find the perimeter of OAPB. (2)
answer_steps: (ii) $PB = 12$ m, because tangents from an external point are equal.
(iii) Area $= 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 60$ m². OR Perimeter $= 5 + 12 + 12 + 5 = 34$ m.

questions.question:
A triangular park ABC has a circular fountain of radius 4 m touching all three sides. The fountain touches BC at D, CA at E and AB at F, with BD = 8 m and DC = 6 m.

(i) Name the pairs of equal tangent segments. (1)

(ii) If AF = x, write AB and AC in terms of x. (1)

(iii) Using area $= r \times s$ (where $s$ is the semi-perimeter) and Heron's formula, find x. OR If x = 7, find the perimeter of the park. (2)
answer_steps: (i) $BD = BF$, $CD = CE$, $AE = AF$.
(iii) $4(14 + x) = \sqrt{(14 + x) \cdot x \cdot 6 \cdot 8}$ gives $x = 7$. OR Perimeter $= 15 + 13 + 14 = 42$ m.
